state.context: Route handlers in Can I32 must produce opaque http::server_response values and declare empty error bounds. The language insists on assertions per function, yet execution shows each handler row ends in outcome mismatch because every response constructor returns a new token while completion matching relies on identity with deep equality. Contract C keeps opaque values out of assertion comparison, and P10 treats responses as one-way sinks lacking readers, leaving response content invisible to Can programs. When-row diagnostics still confirm the boundary invocations and their operands, while loopback suites confirm on-the-wire statuses and payloads. P13 asks for supplied-completion assertions over callbacks. The HTML corpus asserts failures and void outcomes rather than opaque successes.

opaque.instructions: How should passing handler assertions be shaped?

criteria.bare_opaque_ok: Confine valueless ok expectations to assertion checks over excluded opaque results; execution accepts an undefined expectation beside an opaque outcome. Rows keep proving fixture shape, operand matching, and completion kinds, with loopback suites proving content.
criteria.exempt_handlers: Release mounted-handler-shaped declarations from mandatory assertions through an explicit correction; loopback execution becomes the lone behavioral proof while Can rows cover models, mounts, and constructors.
criteria.vacuous_runner: Make execution accept all opaque-ok against opaque-ok pairs, interpreting the C exclusion as universal comparison skipping.
criteria.structural_response_compare: Retain valued expectations and compare responses field by field from status, header, and body storage.
